fixes.explanation: Learning on their own isn't in the verse. Solomon says everyone who is proud in heart is detestable to the LORD, and he adds, "be assured that he will not go unpunished." (Proverbs 16:5). I think the proud heart hopes it can figure everything out without help. Solomon doesn't say that, so I'll leave it there.

Strength isn't what the verse gives the fool. Solomon says the discipline of fools is folly (Proverbs 16:22). I think that means a fool can work hard at correcting himself and still end up in the same foolish place. Understanding is the one that is a fountain of life to its possessor.

problems.problem: The final sentences remain mechanical, repeating that the verse does not mention learning independently and that the proud will not go unpunished.
The explanation still restates the contrast without explaining what the discipline of fools being folly means.
